questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: The raw fragment an object mapper reopens
questions.learningObjective: Explain why copying a stored fragment verbatim moves the trust boundary
questions.stem: A mapper reads stored documents and re-emits one field without encoding, describing this as preserving the original content exactly.

answer.exemplar: Encoding is a property of the destination context, not of the value itself. A fragment that sits harmlessly inside a stored string can become markup once the mapper drops it into a page body, so preserving the bytes byte for byte also preserves the chance that the destination will read them as instructions. The mapper should keep the value encoded and let the final, context aware step decide the treatment.

questions.explanation: A written answer should connect the copied fragment to the destination that will read it, since the same characters mean different things in different places. It should also state that the mapper, not the storage, is where encoding belongs.
questions.hint: Name what the destination will do with the copied text.

questions.topic: Where a template engine's default escaping stops
questions.learningObjective: Describe the positions a default escaping rule does not cover
questions.stem: Describe where the default escaping of a template engine stops being enough, in terms of the positions a page can offer.

answer.exemplar: Default escaping is written for the context it was designed for, usually ordinary text inside an element body. It stops being enough the moment the value lands somewhere with different rules, such as a quoted attribute, a URL, a script block, or a style value. answer.exemplar: A stored fragment of markup is a piece of the page that has been saved. questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: A bound value in a position that names a column
questions.learningObjective: Explain the limits of what a bound value can express
questions.stem: Explain, for a reviewer who knows about binding, what a bound value can and cannot do in a statement that names columns.

answer.exemplar: A bound value can stand for a piece of data in a position the statement has already defined, such as a comparison, an inserted value, or a limit. It cannot stand for a column name, a table name, a direction, or an operator, because those are the parts of the statement that say what it means. When the request needs to choose among known columns, the code maps the request value onto a fixed list and binds the value that goes with the chosen column.

questions.explanation: A strong answer separates positions the statement fixes from positions the request may vary within. It should finish with the mapping approach that lets a request choose without naming a column.
questions.hint: Separate what the statement fixes from what it varies.

questions.topic: Where a template engine's default escaping stops
questions.learningObjective: Give a method for locating the default escaping coverage in a page
questions.stem: Describe a method for working out where the default escaping of a template engine applies in a page you did not write.

answer.exemplar: Start by listing every position on the page that holds a value, whether it is element text, a quoted attribute, a URL, a style value or a script block. Then find which of those positions use the default helper and which use a dedicated one or a raw write, since the raw writes are the ones with no protection. Finally, check the dangerous characters of each position against the rule applied there, which shows both the gaps and the places where a stricter rule than needed is in use.

questions.explanation: A strong answer gives an ordered method that finds positions, identifies the rule in each, and compares rules with dangerous characters. It should mention that raw writes are the highest risk spots.

questions.stem: Explain how a team can decide which encoding a value needs when the same value is written to two different destinations.

answer.exemplar: Treat the value as plain data until it reaches the place that writes it, and let each writing place choose the rule for its own context. answer.exemplar: The mapper should treat the stored markup as a fact about the data, not as an instruction, and encode it for the destination it is written into. questions.topic: A bound value in a position that names a column
questions.learningObjective: Explain a safe way for a request to select a column
questions.stem: Explain a way for a request parameter to select a report column safely when the column name itself cannot be bound as a value.

answer.exemplar: Keep a fixed map in the code from a request token to the real column expression, for example a short code for each of the supported measures. The request supplies the token, the code looks the real column up in the map, and the statement is built from the mapped expression with every data value bound as a parameter. The token is a name for a choice, not a piece of statement text, so a token that is not in the map simply selects nothing and is rejected.

questions.explanation: A strong answer describes the map, the lookup and the rejection path, and shows that the request never contributes statement text. It should make clear that the token is a choice rather than a column name.
questions.hint: Turn the request value into a lookup key.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: What binding does and does not decide
questions.learningObjective: Compute the volume of escaped output in a mapped document set
questions.stem: An object mapper emits raw fragments for 60 of its 1200 documents. Each of those 60 documents also holds 3 escaped fields of 40 characters each.
questions.explanation: Sixty documents times 3 fields times 40 characters gives 7200 characters of escaped output. The other 1140 documents carry no fields of this kind in this calculation.
questions.hint: Multiply the document count, the field count and the field length.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: The raw fragment an object mapper reopens
questions.learningObjective: State the precondition for treating stored fragments as markup

stimulus.body: An importer copies one field from each incoming document into a page that lists the documents. The field sometimes contains angle brackets. The page shows them as visible brackets today, and a colleague wants to switch that so the brackets become formatting.

questions.stem: According to the excerpt, what must be true before the brackets can become formatting?

options.text: The importer must copy the fragment as markup, because a page cannot render formatting from encoded text
options.misconception: believes encoding preserves formatting

options.text: The page must stop escaping the field, since the brackets should be read as instructions
options.misconception: thinks turning off escaping is enough

options.text: The source of the fragment must be trusted for markup, because copying it across reopens it in the page
The importer must mark the field as safe, which tells the template to write it as markup
options.misconception: treats a mark as proof of safety

questions.explanation: Turning off the escaping or adding a mark would apply to any value, including hostile ones. The fragment becomes markup only when the application decides that its source is allowed to write markup into this page.
questions.hint: Ask who is allowed to write markup into the page.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: The scope of a data mapper's guarantee
questions.learningObjective: State the full boundary of a mapper contract
questions.stem: A mapper's contract says it converts the fields it knows, copies the rest unchanged, and never invents values.

options.text: It guarantees the result is complete, because the mapper will fill in any field it does not recognise
options.misconception: inverts the never invents rule

options.text: It guarantees the result is correct, because copying the remaining fields preserves their meaning
options.misconception: extends the promise to meaning

options.text: It guarantees the result is safe to show, because the mapper only writes values it recognises
options.misconception: claims a safety promise

options.text: It guarantees structure, faithful copies, and no invented values, but not that the values are correct

questions.explanation: The contract covers three things: the output structure, faithful copies, and the absence of invented values. Whether the values are meaningful or safe to show is left to the layers that understand the content.
questions.hint: List the promises and then what the contract does not promise.
